name: AR5
description: IPCC AR5 WG1 Chapter 8 emission-metric parameters, as used by the Cooper et al. (2020) spreadsheet and DLCAInputData. No carbon-cycle feedback for non-CO2 gases (issue #33).

myhre2013.citation: Myhre, G., et al., 2013: Anthropogenic and Natural Radiative Forcing. In: Climate Change 2013: The Physical Science Basis. IPCC AR5 WG1, Chapter 8 and Supplementary Material 8.SM.

joos2013.citation: Joos, F., et al., 2013: Carbon dioxide and climate impulse response functions for the computation of greenhouse gas metrics: a multi-model analysis. Atmos. Chem. Phys., 13, 2793-2825.

boucher_reddy2008.citation: Boucher, O. and Reddy, M. S., 2008: Climate trade-off between black carbon and carbon dioxide emissions. Energy Policy, 36, 193-200.

trenberth_smith2005.citation: Trenberth, K. E. and Smith, L., 2005: The mass of the atmosphere: a constraint on global analyses. J. Climate, 18, 864-875.

cooper2020.citation: Cooper, S. J. G., Green, R., Hattam, L., Roeder, M., Welfle, A., and McManus, M., 2020: Exploring temporal aspects of climate-change effects due to bioenergy. Biomass and Bioenergy, 142, 105778. Supplementary spreadsheet mmc2.xlsx (v5).

boucher2009.citation: Boucher, O., Friedlingstein, P., Collins, B., and Shine, K. P., 2009: The indirect global warming potential and global temperature change potential due to methane oxidation. Environ. Res. Lett., 4, 044007.

irf_a.where: Multi-model mean IRF fit, as used in AR5 8.SM.11 (Eq. 8.SM.10). a0 is the permanent fraction.

irf_tau.where: Time constants of the decaying pools a1..a3, AR5 8.SM.11 (Eq. 8.SM.10).

radiative_efficiency_scale.where: Cooper et al. 2020 spreadsheet (adj_factor_CO2 in DLCAInputData). Not an IPCC value.
radiative_efficiency_scale.note: Decision D5 on #26: kept so the Cooper reference reproduces. It scales the AR5 RE so that AGWP100(CO2) = 9.17e-14 W m-2 yr kg-1, the AR5 Table 8.A.1 value; without it AGWP100 is 9.194e-14.

molar_mass.where: Cooper et al. 2020 spreadsheet constants (mol_mass_CO2 in DLCAInputData)

o3.where: 8.SM.11.3.2: tropospheric ozone enhances CH4 forcing by 50%

h2o.where: 8.SM.11.3.2: stratospheric water vapour enhances CH4 forcing by 15%

molar_mass.where: Cooper et al. 2020 spreadsheet constants (mol_mass_CH4 in DLCAInputData)

fossil_co2_yield.unit: mol CO2 per mol CH4 removed
fossil_co2_yield.where: Cooper et al. 2020 spreadsheet; Boucher et al. 2009 (to confirm)
fossil_co2_yield.note: Decision D4 on #26. DLCAInputData stores 0.5 * 44/16 = 1.375 kg CO2 per kg CH4, using nominal integer molar masses; the mass conversion is left to the engine (#27).

o3.where: AR5 metrics include no N2O ozone term

molar_mass.where: Cooper et al. 2020 spreadsheet constants (mol_mass_N2O in DLCAInputData)

q.where: Two-box response as used in AR5 8.SM.11.2

d.where: Two-box response as used in AR5 8.SM.11.2

molar_mass_air.where: Mean molar mass of dry air

agwp100_ch4.where: Table 8.A.1, no climate-carbon feedback (value to confirm against the PDF)

agwp100_n2o.where: Table 8.A.1, no climate-carbon feedback (value to confirm against the PDF)
